scenes.text: Different length-width-height triples can form boxes with the same volume when their products agree.
A cuboid has 84 unit cubes and a 3 times 7 base. Find its height. The answer is 4. Equal volumes: 84 divided by (3 times 7) equals 4 layers.
A box at a school fair holds 128 cubes. Its base measures 8 cubes by 4 cubes. What height makes another box with the same volume? Pause the video and think.
